## The decision point: `SmartRouter.match()`

`src/router/smart-router/router.ts:21-59` is where the runtime choice happens. It's a **lazy, one-time selection triggered by the first incoming request**, not at construction time.

How it works:

1. `add()` (`router.ts:13`) doesn't build anything — it just buffers every route into `this.routes` as `[method, path, handler]` tuples.
2. On the first `match()`, it iterates candidate routers in priority order (`router.ts:30-48`). For each one it replays all buffered routes through `router.add(...)` and tries `router.match()`.
3. If that router throws `UnsupportedPathError`, it's skipped and the loop moves to the next candidate (`router.ts:37-42`). Any other error propagates.
4. The first router that survives wins, and SmartRouter permanently steps out of the way: `this.match = router.match.bind(router)` (`router.ts:44`), `this.routers = [router]`, `this.routes = undefined`. Every subsequent request goes straight to the chosen router with zero dispatch overhead.
5. `this.name` becomes e.g. `"SmartRouter + RegExpRouter"` (`router.ts:56`), and `activeRouter` (`router.ts:61`) throws until selection has occurred.

## Which candidates are offered

The candidate list — the actual policy — is set by the constructor of whichever entry point you use:

| Entry | Candidates | Location |
|---|---|---|
| `hono` (default) | `[RegExpRouter, TrieRouter]` | `src/hono.ts:28-32` |
| `hono/quick` | `[LinearRouter, TrieRouter]` | `src/preset/quick.ts:20-22` |
| `hono/tiny` | `PatternRouter` only, no SmartRouter | `src/preset/tiny.ts:18` |

Note `src/hono.ts:29`: `options.router ?? new SmartRouter(...)`. Passing `new Hono({ router: new RegExpRouter() })` bypasses the whole selection mechanism.

## What makes a router opt out

The `UnsupportedPathError` throws are the signal that drives fallback:

- `src/router/reg-exp-router/router.ts:66` — converts an internal `PATH_ERROR` into `UnsupportedPathError(path)`; this is the common case where a route set can't be compiled into a single regex (e.g. conflicting param names at the same position).
- `src/router/linear-router/router.ts:126` and `src/router/pattern-router/router.ts:35` — same signal for their own limitations.

So in the default setup: RegExpRouter is tried first for speed, and TrieRouter acts as the always-works fallback since it never throws that error.

One consequence worth knowing: because selection is deferred to the first request, a route pattern that RegExpRouter can't handle produces no error at registration time — the fallback happens silently on first traffic.
